sources_of_truth.covers: sidebar() builds the left rail only from `## ` headings and `- [text](target)` list items inside wiki/_index.md, so index membership is what decides whether a published page has a rail entry
collect() publishes every wiki/**/*.md outside wiki/raw/ regardless of index membership, so a page missing from the index still publishes as a page
the rail opens with a hardcoded Home entry and closes with a hardcoded `[What is not here](whats-not-here)` entry, outside the section loop
render() suppresses the See also block for _index.md, so the index's own frontmatter `related` list never reaches a reader

the complete set of checks: frontmatter keys, type and status vocabulary, absolute `sources` paths, dead and raw `related` entries, one H1 matching the title, sentence case, em dashes and emojis, British spelling, the gateway terminology, raw paths in prose, dead links, pending figures as warnings, reader drift, paragraph and section length. There is no index-membership check and no once-and-only-once check.
wiki/raw/ is excluded from linting, and 29 pages are the checked set
the install refusal is computed from a memory budget against the smallest available tier; there is no literal 8 GB floor constant in the probe

the landing shape: routing only, prose under each heading before its links, human titles as link text, every published page exactly once in exactly one section, and section order as the reading order for someone meeting the product cold
the type-to-reader-verb table and what each type teaches, which is how a decision record is distinguished from a how-to
the ratified placement: wiki/meeting-your-persona.md takes its name from the `## Meeting your persona` section wiki/_index.md:34 already carries, and becomes the first entry in that section

the inbound-reference table for install-macos.md: wiki/_index.md:31 is a body link that blocks T16 with a `dead-link` error and is owned by T11; the other blocking references belong to T64, T14, T13, T65 and T12

`type: decision-record` at line 4, an abstract written around a seventeen-screen mockup, and the three beats including Give them a memory

open_questions: Should the `## Meeting your persona` prose at wiki/_index.md:36-39 be rewritten as a four-part arc that names the second brain, or held at three parts with wiki/meeting-your-persona.md introduced separately? wiki/first-run.md:24-29 makes the second brain the third beat and wiki/meeting-your-persona.md devotes two of its seven sections to it (lines 124 and 146), but wiki/_index.md:53 already lists The second brain under `## Living with a house`, and wiki/page-types.md:93 forbids a page appearing twice.

Does wiki/first-run.md still belong in the reader-facing `## Meeting your persona` section once the how-to sits above it? It declares `type: decision-record` at line 4 and its abstract at lines 15-17 is written around a seventeen-screen mockup, while wiki/_index.md:84-86 describes `## Looking under the hood` as the engineering record and says a reader who came to use Hearth can stop above that line. Moving it changes the reading order, which the task statement does not ask for, and tasks/docs/tracker.md:208-210 assumes it stays.

If the `## Getting started` prose at wiki/_index.md:24-27 is restated for three pages, what does it say wiki/updates.md is for? updates.md:15-17 states nothing in it is built yet, while wiki/installing.md:247-260 now carries the by-hand update procedure that the index prose clause "how an existing install becomes a newer one" currently sends a reader to updates.md for.

Is the transient orphan acceptable? Between T11 landing and T16 running, wiki/install-macos.md still publishes (scripts/publish_wiki.py:63-76) with no index entry, no rail entry, and, once T12, T13, T64, T14 and T65 also land, no inbound reference at all except the three `sources` entries the linter never resolves. tasks/docs/tracker.md:271 separates these into Phase C and Phase E deliberately, so the question is whether the two should land in one change rather than whether the ordering is wrong.

Should wiki/meeting-your-persona.md be added to the index's frontmatter `related` list at wiki/_index.md:6-9? It would change nothing a reader sees, because scripts/publish_wiki.py:163-166 suppresses the See also block on _index.md, but the list is the only other place in the file where the index names a page, and it currently names getting-started.md, developing.md and whats-not-here.md.
notes:
Tooling: Bash was in my tool set, so both read-only scripts ran from the worktree root on 2026-09-04. `python scripts/lint_wiki.py --warnings` reported 29 pages checked, 0 errors, 196 warnings, none of them on wiki/_index.md. `python scripts/doc_graph.py --json` reported all seven of wiki/meeting-your-persona.md's sections as unique to it, and its `planned` list names only backend/tool-catalog.md:66 and features/house-feed.md:45, neither relevant here. Bash was used for reading and searching only; the sole file written is this artifact, and publish_wiki.py was read rather than run because even `--out` writes.

Sizing: S, matching the dispatch, and the size is now evidence-backed rather than assumed. One page changes and only one. Not XS, because this is not a single mechanical location: removing line 31 is mechanical, but the prose at lines 24-27 and at lines 36-39 each account for their section's link set exactly as it stands today, so both have to be re-derived. Not M, because no second page needs an edit; every other surviving reference to install-macos.md is assigned to T64, T14, T13, T65, T12 or T16 by tasks/docs/tracker.md:1622-1624, and the three reader-facing neighbours already link wiki/meeting-your-persona.md at wiki/installing.md:245, wiki/getting-started.md:102 and wiki/clients/macos.md:145.

Dispatch questions, answered. Where the new page belongs: first in `## Meeting your persona`, ahead of First run. tasks/docs/tracker.md:208-210 rules it, and the corpus supports it independently, since wiki/installing.md:245 and wiki/getting-started.md:102 both route a reader to the how-to while wiki/meeting-your-persona.md:192-193 names First run as the record behind it. What the prose at 36-39 must do: gain a role for the new page, because it currently accounts for exactly the four links the section lists and no more. Whether the prose at 24-27 still describes the set: yes, and better than it does now, because it names three coverage clauses against four links today and removing line 31 makes them correspond one to one; the machine sentence at lines 24-26 stays accurate against wiki/installing.md:49-55 and :74-80. Whether removing line 31 orphans a page: yes, wiki/install-macos.md, deliberately and until T16. Whether the once-and-only-once rule holds: half of it. No page appears twice, and two pages appear zero times, wiki/meeting-your-persona.md and wiki/whats-not-here.md.

Guard rail for the author, from scripts/publish_wiki.py:189-194: the rail hardcodes a `[What is not here](whats-not-here)` entry outside the section loop, so adding wiki/whats-not-here.md to a section list to satisfy wiki/page-types.md:93 would give it two rail entries. Its prose link at wiki/_index.md:95 is the shape that already works.

Type and mode: Fix pairs with affected as the contract expects, and no disagreement was found. `recommended_type` is `landing`, matching the declared `type:` at wiki/_index.md:4; the page's sections route and carry no detail a reader can act on, so wiki/page-types.md:89-94 holds for it.

Known evidence: every location the dispatch cited resolved and read as described. Nothing in it failed to resolve.

Tracker: tasks/docs/tracker.md exists and was read. Its T11 row at lines 1395-1423 records `Open questions: None.`, so all five questions returned here originate from this stage or from the dispatch rather than from the tracker.

Concurrency, and what it did to two citations. Two sibling Phase C tasks landed on other pages while this run was in progress: T64 removed `install-macos.md` from wiki/getting-started.md's `related` list and T14 removed it from wiki/releasing.md's, one deleted line each, confirmed by `git diff --stat` at the end of the run. That shifted wiki/getting-started.md's line numbers up by one after line 8. Every citation in this artifact is the post-edit state, re-read after the change: the prose link to the new page is at wiki/getting-started.md:102, its `related` entry at :8 and its `sources` entry at :22. The repo-wide `install-macos` grep quoted in the claims was taken before those two edits, so it still lists wiki/getting-started.md:8 and wiki/releasing.md:9; both are now cleared and neither was ever T11's. Nothing in wiki/_index.md changed during the run.
